notes:
Context: Northbridge runs a real-time ad bidding and personalization stack; inference must be tightly coupled to auction windows (sub-100ms decision preferred for initial scoring, streaming token generation acceptable for longer personalization).

Main ask: a formal throughput guarantee for Dedicated capacity. Negotiation points below.

Targets discussed (customer asks / Redwood proposals):
- Customer: sustained aggregate min 250k tokens/sec across reserved pool during business hours (08:00-20:00 NA), with 95th-percentile per-request latency <= 300ms for single-token streams.
- Customer: concurrency cap expectations: norm 60 concurrent scoring sessions, occasional bursts to 220 concurrent sessions for up to 45s during campaign launches.
- Customer favors hard concurrency caps mapped to per-tenant queues + prioritized burst buckets.
- Preferred reserved hardware: initial commit 8xH100 (or equivalent capacity) with option to expand to 16 in Q3. Customer asked Redwood to price both H100 and A100 configs.

Redwood proposals / internal options discussed:
- Min tokens/sec guarantee framed as a contract SLA: baseline sustained tokens/sec (e.g., 200k sustained across pool) + defined burst capacity (2x sustained for up to 60s) before best-effort throttling.
- Concurrency caps implemented as per-shard soft limits + token-leaky bucket to ensure fair share; hard caps only applied after agreed burst window.
- Latency SLOs tied to routing policy: P50 target 120-150ms, P95 target <= 300ms for 1-token streaming responses when routing to dedicated pool. Falls back to hosted lower-cost model with higher latency on overload.
negotiation_points: Define 'sustained' (time window) for tokens/sec SLA - customer prefers 5m sliding window; Redwood proposed 1m and 5m windows with different tiers
Burst policy: length, multiplier, and preemption procedure for bursts - need clarity on penalty credits if bursts exceed SLA
Measurement: which metrics count toward SLA (aggregate tokens/sec vs per-tenant throughput) and telemetry visibility into token accounting
Capacity buffer & reservation: how many GPUs reserved vs hot-plug burst capacity (billing for reserved vs burst)
Failure modes: agreed fallback flow (model variant, region fallback) and compensation for degraded throughput/latency
